digest.component_or_area: epic-close verification gate (DET floor + bug screen + verifier adjudication)
propositions: Agents file bugs outside epic hierarchy and mark them out-of-scope when they are defects in the epic's own deliverable; the direct-children close gate cannot detect these undispositioned escapes (observed: 2 real at-close escapes in 56-epic backtest).

A deterministic floor stage must block epic close when any open/in_progress bug carries a caused_by edge pointing to the epic or its descendants, teaching agents to fix, re-parent, or dispute the link.

A candidate filter (open/in_progress bugs created after epic's first in_progress transition OR linked any-relation any-depth to the subtree) feeds at most 32 bugs to a haiku screen; overflow is recorded in the sidecar.

A haiku relevance screen (single forced-choice A/B/C verdict per candidate: defect-in-deliverable / pre-existing-sibling / unrelated) forwards A-verdicts as compact evidence (≤8 rows) to the verifier inside the precheck-assembled fenced context.

The verifier blocks only undispositioned deliverable-defects; a disposition satisfies via store-grounded signals: (a) supersedes or duplicates link in the epic subtree or successor, or (b) reasoned pre-existence/deferral prose in bug description/comments (bare 'out of scope' does not qualify).

Screen runs through model-class config (TRIVIAL_CLASS + resolve_model_string()) with shared cache settings, warm-then-fan-out orchestration; screen tally (verdict + citation per bug + overflow count) recorded in completion sidecar; screen failure degrades open (logged) never blocks.
